note: the posted-comment exclusion is a line-proximity match (same kind + path, ±2 lines), the same tolerance `acceptable` uses. Two different gaps of the same kind within 2 lines of each other would collapse into one candidate. That under-counts an FP rather than inventing one, so it errs the right way for a precision metric. If it ever matters, match by `obligation_ids` when both sides carry them.

note: the dogfood's low-confidence finding is fair. The renamed-away branch (`previous_filename === file` → deleted marker → null) has no test. It matches post.js's `--no-renames` behaviour, so it is not a bug. A one-line case in the existing `apiGit` test would pin it. Not blocking.

Review against S9/S10 from the supplement.

- S10: a weak/missing coverage row with no item or comment now counts once per F29 group and breaks expect_clean. Your extra test caught a real double count (row + posted comment = 2 FPs), which is the useful kind of review finding.
- S9: the weekly report now asks post.js's own `anchorTouched`/`testsChanged` through an API-backed git stand-in. One rule, not a second copy. Every failure path ends as null (unknown), never false, and the truncated-compare case is pinned.
- `unified0` is checked against real `git diff -U0` headers for add, delete, modify, two runs and no-newline.
- S9 and S10 tests fail on main; the posted-comment test is honestly labelled a control.
- Dogfood ran the model (status incomplete: reduced fast tier), so the re-set key works.

P3: `TITLE` is interpolated into a RegExp unescaped. That is safe today because it is a constant with no metacharacters, but a later wording change (e.g. adding `(beta)` or `?`) would silently break the foreign check, and every issue would look "ours" again. Escape it (`TITLE.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&')`) or compare with `startsWith(TITLE + ': ')` and parse the rest. Either way it's a one-liner.
